description: Recorded tool-call script for ECII Test E (generalization), a cooling fan module integrated into an electronic enclosure, replayed by the FAKE provider. It proves the same structure for an unrelated domain, with the host identified and owned by the project, so its readiness differs from the sensor script. It is not a model run and says nothing about reasoning quality. Domain words appear here as fixture values only.

turns.user: ^Design a cooling fan module that integrates into my electronic enclosure

arguments.rationale: The module is installed inside an enclosure that belongs to the same project, so it is embedded in an identified system.

externalSystems.name: Electronic enclosure (project design)
externalSystems.description: The enclosure designed in this project; its walls, vents and card guides are project data.

objectives: Move air through the enclosure to keep electronics within temperature limits

informationNeeds.text: Pattern and size of the module mounting holes
informationNeeds.subject: sys-1

arguments.reason: ECII Test E: interpret the intent before designing

steps.final: I interpreted this as a component embedded in an enclosure from this project; the host is identified and owned by the project. Apply the intent to record it. I have not designed anything yet.

arguments.text: Ways to integrate a cooling fan module into an electronic enclosure
arguments.name: Fan integration architectures

alternatives.name: Slot-in module on card guides
alternatives.summary: The module slides into card guides the enclosure already has.

architecture.interfaceGeometry: Guide spacing and slot depth come from the enclosure design
assumptions: A free card slot is available (unverified)
architecture.attachmentPrinciple: Module slides into guides and locks with a latch
architecture.loadPath: Module weight rests in the guides; airflow reaction is carried by the latch
architecture.installationRemoval: Slide in until the latch clicks; release the latch to remove
evidenceRequired: Free slot position and guide dimensions from the enclosure model

alternatives.name: Screwed to the wall at a vent opening
alternatives.summary: The module is screwed to the inside of a wall around a vent.

architecture.hostInterface: A vent opening in an enclosure wall
architecture.interfaceGeometry: Opening size and screw positions come from the enclosure design
assumptions: The opening is large enough for the chosen module (unverified)
architecture.attachmentPrinciple: Module frame fastened around the opening with screws
architecture.loadPath: Module weight and vibration pass through the screws into the wall
architecture.installationRemoval: Fasten from inside; unscrew to remove
disadvantages: Needs access to the inside of the wall
evidenceRequired: Opening size and wall thickness from the enclosure model

alternatives.name: Hinged panel replacing a blanking plate
alternatives.summary: A hinged panel carrying the module replaces a blanking plate.

architecture.hostInterface: A blanking plate position on the enclosure front
architecture.interfaceGeometry: Plate position and frame size come from the enclosure design
risks: Dust ingress at the panel edge
assumptions: The blanking plate can be replaced (unverified)
architecture.attachmentPrinciple: Hinged panel with the module, closed against the enclosure frame
architecture.loadPath: Module weight is carried by the hinge and the closing latch
architecture.installationRemoval: Swing open for service; the panel unhooks from the hinge
evidenceRequired: Front frame dimensions and sealing needs

steps.final: I prepared three different ways to integrate the fan module into the enclosure; each names the feature it depends on and the evidence needed, and none states a dimension I do not know. Apply to record them.
